questions.answer: On campus

questions.answer: different dorm types with different numbers of roomies.

questions.answer: Convenient, relatively cheap but also very boring given the part of the city campus is at.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very difficult. Everything sorted out in the day. But stressful!!! at the start. bad system.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to preselect courses. But don't expect to get many/any of them. Then there is a add/drop deadline 2 weeks into the semester, this means people will drop a lot of extra courses that they have taken even though they are planning on taking them, which then leaves space for you to join. This however also means you will have to follow some courses you are not yet assigned to for the first 2 weeks.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only guides. A lot of contact with go global, who answered relatively fast. They were flexible. Professors also answered mails and did what they could to help out in general.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Ended up getting 5/5 I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: it all works out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Obv. lower level that at KU. However, I found professors were MUCH more engaged and inspiring.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 2x 400 level courses and 3x 300 level courses. 300 level where similar to what I did 1. year at KU. 400 courses were however sort of like a natural extension of 3rd year stuff back home, similar to what I would have done on 6th semester in ECON.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lecture based. More intuition less math. Not as in-depth.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 441: The Process of Economic Development
ECON 421: Introduction to Game Theory and Appliances
ECON 335: Demography, Human migration and Families.
ECON 305: Honours Intermediate Macroeconomic Analysis II
ECON 371: Economics of the environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ECON 441: The process of economic development. Amazing approach, great prof, great subject. Important state-of-the-art papers on culture, institutions and how they shape economies.

ECON 421: Game Theory. Good and fun

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ended up going a lot to the US. 4 times in total to visit Yellowstone, LA, San Francisco and Seattle. Those trips were obv. very expensive. Skiing is also super expensive here.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out and food. Vancouver (Canada) is super cheap. A lot to do with current exchange rate though

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts! Literally anything. I was a part of the Surf club, Outdoors club and Ski club. First and last also great for hosting house parties. And first two have great trips. Especially try to go to Rock party - a 3 night weekend in Squamish with rock climbing (with instructors) with 300 people, sleeping in tents and partying with DJ's and barbecues and such.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go hiking all the time! rent a car. Get out there fist and every weekend. skip class. Make every weekend extended and sleep in your rented car on parking lots. Get cheap flights to the US if you don't mind flying a bit since you're here - especially when Vancouver weather starts getting bad.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Whistler and Squamish are just the best for outdoor activities. Try to go to Banff early as well (or when it's warm)! Also great in winter for skiing though. Vancouver Island is super cool. Explore it and see whales and bears and such.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Also helps its convenient and that people are open and easygoing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are quite young and many are very boring tbh.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Boring campus life outside of specific clubs.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Asian food in Vancouver is best outside of Asia by far.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Consider bringing tent and such from back home. You will probably use it all. Otherwise join Varsity Outdoor Club, then you can rent gear for free.
Plan weekends well in advance if you consider doing big trips.
Don't but groceries on campus, go to No Frills (like netto)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: consider not living on campus if you can afford it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Nature is wild here! doing outdoorsy stuff all the time will be missed so bad

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Cultural differences with roomies on cleaning. Missing people from back home - It is VERY far from Denmark. Not easy to get visitors.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
